speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Manpower what can be done to reduce the amount of unclaimed CPF monies going forward.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether CPF Board will consider changing the CPF nomination process to facilitate more seamless distribution of deceased CPF members' funds to their loved ones and rightful owners promptly.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
text: asked the Minister for Manpower regarding unclaimed CPF monies (a) what are the profiles of these members by age, ethnic group, marital status and education level; (b) what measures does the Ministry have to increase the awareness of nominations, such as that of contacting and engaging those above a certain age who have yet to make nominations; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider allowing higher withdrawal amounts for those who have no kin to nominate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are several key issues I hope to address in this reply.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The first question is whether most Central Provident Fund (CPF) monies go unclaimed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The vast majority of deceased members had made nominations as to who they wish to receive their unused CPF monies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Their monies were distributed to beneficiaries according to these nominations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is typically done within a month of CPF Board being notified of the member's passing by the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority and where the nominees’ bank details have been submitted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked about the profile of those who nominated, compared to those who did not.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But even if a member did not make a nomination for anyone to receive his unused CPF monies, it may still be distributed to his next-of-kin according to the intestacy and Muslim inheritance laws.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: CPF Board will pass the monies to PTO typically within three weeks of notification of the member’s passing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: PTO will then trace and search for the next-of-kin.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Ministry of Law (MinLaw) will be answering a separate question on the efforts taken to return the un-nominated CPF monies to members’ next-of-kin.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The second question is whether unclaimed CPF monies are then forfeited.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As MinLaw will explain in greater detail, the next-of-kin can approach PTO at any time to submit their claims.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is no time limit for them to do so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The third question is whether CPF Board makes an effort to reduce the incidence of unclaimed monies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: First, educating members; second, reminding members regularly; and third, making it easy for members to nominate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: CPF Board raises awareness on the importance of making a CPF nomination through annual island-wide CPF roadshows.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It also works with other industry stakeholders, such as lawyers and insurance agents, to advise their clients on making a CPF nomination.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If one has been made, CPF Board also lets the member know when the nomination was made, in case the member wants to change his mind.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members may be aware that CPF Board runs a CPF Retirement Planning Service for members before they reach age 55, and a second time before they reach age 65.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At these planning sessions, if a member has not already made a nomination, the CPF Board officer will remind the member.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Thirdly, as Ms Foo Mee Har alluded to in her question, CPF Board strives to make it easy for members to nominate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the CPF Retirement Planning Service, if a member decides to make a nomination, it can be done on the spot.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, a nomination can be made in-person at any of the CPF Service Centres or via post.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To Mr Chong Kee Hiong’s question, what if a member has no next-of-kin, for members on the Retirement Sum Scheme, the payouts are computed taking into consideration life expectancy, which is unrelated to whether a person has next-of-kin.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, such members may wish to join the CPF LIFE scheme and choose the Standard Plan which generally offers higher payouts for life.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: After all, they have no next-of-kin to fall back on if they outlive their savings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At the same time, we focus on helping every member get their nominations done well in advance.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am quite sure, in terms of CPF going out to encourage everyone to make nominations, this has been ongoing.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The fact is that there is still 2% of CPF members who have yet to make nominations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: From the Minister's earlier answers, it appears that it is the younger ones who have not made nominations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I wonder and I would like to ask the Minister whether 2% – it does not appear as a big number – but when you aggregate it across, it could be 30,000, 40,000 members who have not made nominations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Would the Minister consider making it such that nominations are almost automatic?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For those who are not married, perhaps, could it automatically go to their parents?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Just to make it even easier, if they choose to make new nominations, that could be done at the time that the member chooses to do so, as against now – notwithstanding all the reminders, statements to inform the CPF members that they have not made a nomination – it goes unnoticed and it remains a case where they have not made a nomination.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, where there is actually someone that you can give the money to, even if the person did not make the nomination, that is not the most difficult thing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The most difficult thing is where there is a next-of-kin but we have difficulty tracing them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The correct thing to do is, therefore, to make sure that the monies are never forfeited.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The person could be overseas, the next-of-kin may have lost touch with the deceased member and may not even be aware that the person has passed away and that there is unused CPF monies to be distributed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is a very small group where even with the best efforts, the Public Trustee's Office will have difficulty tracing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The question of how to deal with this group is not so much a matter of nomination, it is whether we can find more effective ways to do the trace and search.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is also another question that has been posed to MinLaw and I would like to suggest that perhaps we can let MinLaw answer that question and then we can follow up.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, the Minister mentioned about the roadshow to inform people about the nomination.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second supplementary question is that my colleague Ms Foo Mee Har had also in October this year raised the question on whether MOM could increase the payout under the Retirement Sum Scheme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We already do so, through the yearly Statement of Account.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, at the end of the day, I am also mindful that people need to think a little bit about who they wish to nominate and the appropriate thing to do, therefore, is that when they are ready to do so and to enable them to do so in a seamless manner.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: From the statistics, it is quite clear that it is the younger individuals who may not have thought so much about it and, therefore, they have not made a nomination.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What we intend to do is to make this nomination process even easier for younger persons who are very tech savvy through a technology platform.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I am hopeful that it will help to promote nominations.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We do understand, of course, if the member died in Singapore, there is a death certificate issued and CPF Board is quite efficient actually in notifying the beneficiaries.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But is there any inter-governmental procedure if the person were to die overseas?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Do governments frequently exchange information about deaths of nationals that have occurred overseas that may be relevant to Singaporeans dying, say, in Cambodia or Thailand, for example?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But, most likely, it is the next-of-kin who would trigger the payouts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Ms Sylvia Lim explained, usually, it is quite efficient.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But if she is aware of any specific cases where these disbursements have not been done in a timely manner, I invite her to let me know about it and I would be happy to look into that.
